label: <DEL> step of long sequences / sequences starting with w,0,i,a,o,u,q
predicate: (phase == 1) & ((isin(first_tok, [tok("w"), tok("0"), tok("i"), tok("a"), tok("o"), tok("u"), tok("q")]) & (L >= 6)) | (L == 9))
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (t == L, input <DEL>, about to output the first original token); never on original or copy steps. Only about 13% of delimiter steps cross the threshold, and which ones looks like a graded sum of two factors. (1) Sequence length: the rate rises steeply with L (0.3% at L=3, 33% at L=9), and L=9 holds about half the mass. (2) The first original token (the one about to be output): w is strongest (18% of mass), then 0, i, a, o, u, q. The largest activations are long sequences that start with w or 0 (e.g. w w y h f g s r <DEL>). Tokens near the end (prev_tok r/f/s/p) have only a weak effect. No crisp boundary: many L=9 delimiter steps stay inactive, and short sequences with other first tokens sometimes fire weakly. Precision is the main limitation.
